question: Who are our most engaged organizations?

events.question: Who are our most engaged organizations?

intent.status: Mapped organizations and events for engagement

events.label: Mapped organizations and events for engagement

plan.headline: Rank organizations by activity in the period, counting distinct active users and feature usage, excluding test and internal accounts.

metrics.title: Most engaged organizations
metrics.description: Top organizations ranked by number of feature_used events in the selected period, shown with distinct active users, logins, and distinct features used. Only events from non-excluded orgs and users are counted.

metrics.title: Share of orgs highly engaged
metrics.description: Percent of non-test organizations with at least the minimum number of active days in the period. An active day is a day with at least one event from a user in the org.

metrics.title: Weekly active organizations
metrics.description: Count of distinct organizations with at least one event each week over the selected period, to show whether engagement is growing or shrinking.

assumptions.label: Date range
assumptions.rationale: Engagement is measured over a recent window; 90 days smooths out weekly noise.

assumptions.label: Timezone
assumptions.rationale: Days and weeks are bucketed in UTC since orgs span many home timezones.

assumptions.label: Exclude test orgs
assumptions.rationale: The data dictionary says QA, demo and load-test tenants should be excluded from business metrics.

assumptions.label: Exclude internal users
assumptions.rationale: Events from our own staff (users.is_internal) would inflate customer engagement.

assumptions.label: Engagement measure
assumptions.rationale: Ranking basis for the table; feature usage reflects real product value more than logins, which are once per session.

assumptions.label: Orgs to show
assumptions.rationale: A short ranked list is easy to scan and act on.

assumptions.label: Min active days
assumptions.rationale: An org counts as highly engaged if active on at least this many distinct days in the period.

events.sql: WITH orgs AS (SELECT o.id FROM northwind.organizations o WHERE (NOT :exclude_test_accounts::boolean OR NOT o.is_test)), active_days AS (SELECT e.org_id, count(DISTINCT (e.occurred_at AT TIME ZONE :timezone::text)::date) AS days FROM northwind.events e JOIN northwind.users u ON u.id = e.user_id JOIN orgs ON orgs.id = e.org_id WHERE e.occurred_at >= (:date_range_start::date)::timestamp AT TIME ZONE :timezone::text AND e.occurred_at < (:date_range_end::date)::timestamp AT TIME ZONE :timezone::text AND (NOT :exclude_internal_users::boolean OR NOT u.is_internal) GROUP BY e.org_id) SELECT round(100.0 * count(*) FILTER (WHERE ad.days >= :engaged_min_days::int) / NULLIF(count(*), 0), 1) AS value FROM orgs LEFT JOIN active_days ad ON ad.org_id = orgs.id
events.explanation: Percent of in-scope orgs (test excluded per toggle) having at least the minimum distinct active days (events from non-internal users) in the period, in the chosen timezone.

events.sql:
WITH weeks AS (
  SELECT generate_series(date_trunc('week', (:date_range_start::date)::timestamp), date_trunc('week', ((:date_range_end::date) - 1)::timestamp), interval '1 week') AS wk
), ev AS (
  SELECT date_trunc('week', e.occurred_at at time zone :timezone::text) AS wk, e.org_id
  FROM northwind.events e
  JOIN northwind.organizations o ON o.id = e.org_id
  JOIN northwind.users u ON u.id = e.user_id
  WHERE e.occurred_at >= (:date_range_start::date)::timestamp at time zone :timezone::text
    AND e.occurred_at < (:date_range_end::date)::timestamp at time zone :timezone::text
    AND (NOT :exclude_test_accounts::boolean OR o.is_test = false)
    AND (NOT :exclude_internal_users::boolean OR u.is_internal = false)
), counts AS (
  SELECT wk, count(DISTINCT org_id) AS active_orgs FROM ev GROUP BY wk
)
SELECT w.wk::date AS x, COALESCE(c.active_orgs, 0) AS y
FROM weeks w
LEFT JOIN counts c ON c.wk = w.wk
ORDER BY x
events.explanation: Counts distinct orgs with any event per week (in the chosen timezone) within the date range, excluding test orgs and internal users per the toggles, filling empty weeks with 0.

events.sql: WITH ev AS (SELECT e.org_id, e.user_id, e.type, e.feature, (e.occurred_at AT TIME ZONE :timezone::text)::date AS d FROM northwind.events e JOIN northwind.organizations o ON o.id = e.org_id JOIN northwind.users u ON u.id = e.user_id WHERE e.occurred_at >= (:date_range_start::date)::timestamp AT TIME ZONE :timezone::text AND e.occurred_at < (:date_range_end::date)::timestamp AT TIME ZONE :timezone::text AND (NOT :exclude_test_accounts::boolean OR o.is_test = false) AND (NOT :exclude_internal_users::boolean OR u.is_internal = false)), agg AS (SELECT org_id, count(*) FILTER (WHERE type = 'feature_used') AS feature_events, count(DISTINCT user_id) AS active_users, count(DISTINCT d) AS active_days, count(*) FILTER (WHERE type = 'login') AS logins, count(DISTINCT feature) FILTER (WHERE type = 'feature_used') AS distinct_features FROM ev GROUP BY org_id) SELECT o.name AS organization, a.feature_events, a.active_users, a.active_days, a.logins, a.distinct_features FROM agg a JOIN northwind.organizations o ON o.id = a.org_id ORDER BY CASE :engagement_measure::text WHEN 'feature_events' THEN a.feature_events WHEN 'active_users' THEN a.active_users WHEN 'active_days' THEN a.active_days WHEN 'logins' THEN a.logins END DESC, a.feature_events DESC, o.name LIMIT LEAST(:top_n::int, 50)
events.explanation: Aggregates in-period events (excluding test orgs/internal users per toggles) per org, then ranks by the chosen engagement measure and returns the top N (capped at 50 rows).

review.summary: The weekly active org counts are correct, but the first and last weeks are partial and will show misleading dips at both ends of the trend line, so the rewrite plots only complete weeks.

issues.message: date_range_start 2026-07-31 falls on a Friday and date_range_end runs past the 2026-10-27 data cutoff. The first week (Jul 27) and last week (Oct 26) of the generate_series therefore cover only 2–3 days and undercount distinct org_id; limit the series to complete Monday-start weeks.

review.rewritten_sql:
WITH bounds AS (
  SELECT date_trunc('week', ((:date_range_start::date) + 6)::timestamp) AS first_wk,
         date_trunc('week', (:date_range_end::date)::timestamp) - interval '1 week' AS last_wk
), weeks AS (
  SELECT generate_series(b.first_wk, b.last_wk, interval '1 week') AS wk FROM bounds b
), ev AS (
  SELECT date_trunc('week', e.occurred_at at time zone :timezone::text) AS wk, e.org_id
  FROM northwind.events e
  JOIN northwind.organizations o ON o.id = e.org_id
  JOIN northwind.users u ON u.id = e.user_id
  WHERE e.occurred_at >= (:date_range_start::date)::timestamp at time zone :timezone::text
    AND e.occurred_at < (:date_range_end::date)::timestamp at time zone :timezone::text
    AND (NOT :exclude_test_accounts::boolean OR o.is_test = false)
    AND (NOT :exclude_internal_users::boolean OR u.is_internal = false)
), counts AS (
  SELECT wk, count(DISTINCT org_id) AS active_orgs FROM ev GROUP BY wk
)
SELECT w.wk::date AS x, COALESCE(c.active_orgs, 0) AS y
FROM weeks w
LEFT JOIN counts c ON c.wk = w.wk
ORDER BY x
